settings.installText: Install Journey Studio as a real PWA. This creates the application identity used by Windows and the browser. Do not use downloaded Internet Shortcut (.url/.download) files as the app shortcut.
settings.installInstalledText: The app is running with the installed PWA identity.
settings.installUnavailable: The browser install prompt is not currently available. Use your browser's Install app command if it supports installable web apps.
settings.installNote: First time on each Windows PC: install the Windows helper once. After that, Create desktop shortcut creates a real Journey Studio.lnk in one click.
settings.shortcutText: With Journey Studio Windows Helper this action can actually create a real Windows .lnk shortcut to the installed Journey Studio app.
settings.helperNoAdminText: The helper installs only for your Windows user under LocalAppData and HKCU. It does not use PowerShell.
settings.helperStep1: First time only: download the Windows helper once on each PC.
settings.helperStep2: Double-click Install-Journey-Studio-Helper.vbs. It registers the helper and immediately creates Journey Studio.lnk on the desktop.
settings.helperStep3: After that, simply press Create shortcut now. The helper copies the real installed PWA shortcut from the Start menu to the desktop and applies the JS icon.
settings.helperLaunchStatus: The Windows helper was called. If your browser asks permission to open Journey Studio Helper, choose Open.
settings.helperNote: Journey Studio must be installed as an app/PWA first. The helper does not create a web shortcut; it copies the installed Windows app shortcut and saves it as Journey Studio.lnk.
settings.helperWindowsOnly: Automatic desktop shortcut creation is available on Windows. Other platforms use their normal app or dock controls.
nodeDesc.trigger: What starts or reactivates the journey, such as a search, need, event or prior action.
nodeDesc.need: The underlying customer need or job to be done that explains why the journey matters.
nodeDesc.audienceSegment: Who this node or branch applies to, such as geography, customer status or an intent audience.
nodeDesc.customerStep: A concrete customer action or state in the journey that is not itself a channel or conversion.
nodeDesc.decision: A choice, evaluation or branch point, for example buy/not buy or eligible/not eligible.
nodeDesc.meta: A paid or organic customer touchpoint on Meta platforms.
nodeDesc.googleAds: A paid search, Performance Max or other Google Ads customer touchpoint.
nodeDesc.landingPage: A website page or content destination where the customer continues the journey.
nodeDesc.shopCheckout: A cart, product shop or checkout step where purchase intent becomes transactional.
nodeDesc.physicalVisit: An offline visit or real-world experience that changes the next best action.
nodeDesc.cta: The explicit action the customer is asked to take, such as Buy ticket or Upgrade.
nodeDesc.tracking: A measurable event or signal used to observe progress or build audiences.
nodeDesc.conversion: The completed B2C business outcome, such as a purchase, upgrade or reactivation.
nodeDesc.lead: A submitted enquiry or lead before final qualification or booking.
nodeDesc.booking: A confirmed booking or sale that closes a booking-led journey.
nodeDesc.exclusion: A rule that removes people from irrelevant communication, campaigns or audiences.
nodeDesc.crm: A first-party CRM or email touchpoint before or after conversion.
nodeDesc.note: A strategic rule, explanation or context that should be visible in the journey without representing a customer action.
inspector.backgroundColorHelp: Soft tints preserve contrast and readability for text, badges and icons.
